Not applicable - given by deep intramuscular injection
Used to terminate 2nd-trimester pregnancy; not for viable fetus; embryotoxic

summary: Carboprost tromethamine is the tromethamine salt of 15-methyl prostaglandin F2-alpha, a potent oxytocic agent given by deep intramuscular injection. It stimulates strong, sustained myometrial contractions resembling term labor, evacuating the gravid uterus and, postpartum, producing hemostasis at the placental site. Its principal modern use is treatment of postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony that has not responded to oxytocin, uterine massage and ergot preparations; it is also licensed to induce abortion between the 13th and 20th weeks of gestation. Gastrointestinal effects (vomiting, diarrhea, nausea) and transient fever are common and frequently mitigated by pretreatment with antiemetics and antidiarrheals. It must be used only by trained personnel in a setting with intensive-care and surgical backup.
indications: Treatment of postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony not responsive to conventional management (oxytocin, uterine massage and, unless contraindicated, IM ergot preparations)
Aborting pregnancy between the 13th and 20th weeks of gestation (calculated from first day of last normal menses)
Failure of expulsion of the fetus during treatment by another method (second-trimester abortion)
Premature or inadvertent rupture of membranes with insufficient/absent uterine activity, or need for repeat intrauterine instillation, in second-trimester abortion

dosage.t: Single; may repeat at 15-90 min intervals
dosage.n: Most successful cases respond to a single injection; max total ~2 mg (8 doses)

dosage.d: Initial 250 mcg (1 mL) deep IM; optional 100 mcg (0.4 mL) test dose
dosage.t: Repeat 250 mcg q1.5-3.5 h per uterine response
dosage.n: May increase to 500 mcg (2 mL) if contractility inadequate after several 250 mcg doses

dosage.d: Do not exceed 12 mg total dose
dosage.t: Do not give continuously for more than 2 days
dosage.n: Use a tuberculin syringe for accurate small-volume dosing

admin: Administer by deep intramuscular injection using a tuberculin syringe for accuracy
Use only by medically trained personnel in a hospital with immediate intensive-care and acute surgical facilities
Pretreat or co-administer antiemetic and antidiarrheal agents to reduce the high incidence of GI effects
Refrigerate the product at 2-8 C until use
Any failed pregnancy termination must be completed by another method (drug is not a feticidal agent)
moa: Carboprost is a synthetic 15-methyl analogue of prostaglandin F2-alpha with greater potency and a longer duration than the natural prostaglandin. Administered intramuscularly it stimulates myometrial contractions in the gravid uterus similar to term labor contractions, evacuating the products of conception, and postpartum produces myometrial contraction that gives hemostasis at the placental site. It also stimulates gastrointestinal smooth muscle (causing vomiting and diarrhea) and can raise body temperature and, at large doses, blood pressure through vascular smooth-muscle contraction.

absolute: Hypersensitivity (including anaphylaxis and angioedema) to carboprost tromethamine
Active cardiac, pulmonary, renal or hepatic disease
Use when the fetus in utero has reached viability
relative: History of asthma or bronchospastic disease
Diabetes, anemia, jaundice or compromised uterine scar/prior uterine surgery
monitor: Patients receiving other oxytocic agents (augmented activity - concomitant use not recommended)
Patients with febrile illness (drug-induced fever can confound infection diagnosis)

preg: Carboprost is used specifically to terminate pregnancy in the second trimester and is not indicated once the fetus has reached viability; it should not be considered a feticidal agent. Animal studies do not indicate it is teratogenic but it is embryotoxic in rats and rabbits, and any dose producing increased uterine tone could endanger an embryo or fetus. A previable fetus aborted by carboprost may exhibit transient life signs.
lact: Carboprost is given as single or short-course injections in the immediate obstetric setting (e.g. postpartum hemorrhage). Excretion into human milk has not been well characterized; given its short half-life and the acute clinical need, breastfeeding can generally continue, with infant observation.
renal: Contraindicated in patients with active renal disease. No specific dosage adjustment is described because use is acute and short-term in patients without significant renal impairment.
hepatic: Contraindicated in patients with active hepatic disease. No specific dosage adjustment is described for acute obstetric use in patients without significant hepatic impairment.

major: Other oxytocic agents (oxytocin, ergometrine, other prostaglandins) - carboprost augments their activity; concomitant use is not recommended
moderate: Drugs that lower seizure threshold may add to risk in susceptible patients during fever/contraction-related stress
minor: No clinically significant minor interactions specifically characterized
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction relevant to acute single-setting use.
interactions.diagnostics: Drug-induced transient fever may be mistaken for infection (e.g. endometritis); temperature elevations usually resolve within hours of the last injection.

serious: Excessive uterine activity leading to uterine rupture
rare: Septic shock or uterine perforation in the abortion setting

monitoring: Uterine tone and amount of vaginal bleeding (response to therapy)
Respiratory status / oxygenation, particularly in patients with reactive airways
Need for and timing of repeat doses determined by the attending physician based on clinical course
counsel: This is a hospital-administered injection used to control heavy bleeding after delivery or to assist pregnancy termination
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, flushing, shivering and a brief rise in temperature are common and usually short-lived
Medicines to reduce nausea and diarrhea may be given alongside it
Tell staff immediately about chest tightness, wheezing or trouble breathing
pk: Uterine contractions begin within minutes of IM injection
Rapid myometrial stimulation following deep IM administration
Short; activity managed by repeated dosing at defined intervals
Sustained contractile effect requiring repeat dosing per uterine response
pearls: Second-line uterotonic for postpartum hemorrhage - use after oxytocin, uterine massage and ergometrine have failed
Avoid in asthma/reactive airway disease because of the risk of bronchospasm
Routinely pretreat with an antiemetic and antidiarrheal to blunt the prominent GI effects
Total dose must not exceed 12 mg and the drug should not be given continuously beyond 2 days
Transient fever is a known drug effect, but endometritis must still be excluded in the abortion setting
missed: Carboprost is administered by a clinician in an acute hospital setting on a response-driven schedule, so there is no patient-managed missed dose. Timing and need for repeat doses are decided by the attending physician based on uterine response and bleeding.
overdose: Overdose may produce exaggerated pharmacologic effects: severe vomiting and diarrhea, marked uterine hyperstimulation with risk of rupture, hypertension, bronchospasm and high fever. There is no specific antidote; discontinue the drug and provide supportive care including airway/respiratory support, fluid and electrolyte replacement, and treatment of bronchospasm and hypertension.
